html:
Chikashsha Yaki is the homeland of the Chickasaw, a Muskogean people of what is now northern Mississippi, western Tennessee and nearby Alabama. They farmed maize, beans and squash in towns on the uplands and hunted deer across a wide range.

In the winter of 1540 to 1541 Hernando de Soto camped among them; when he demanded porters, they burned his camp. In the 1700s they were known as the strongest warriors in the region and allies of the English, and they defeated French armies in the Chickasaw Wars of the 1730s. Their kin and frequent rivals were the Choctaw.

Under the Treaty of Pontotoc Creek in 1832 they sold their land, and in 1837 most moved west on the Trail of Tears, settling in Indian Territory. See Chickasaw (Oklahoma) for the nation there today.
